messages:
meera: Quick idea: instead of point prefetch hints, what if we have a predictive warmup coordinator that batches warmup signals across the scheduler and ranks page ranges by probability? Could reduce duplicate IO for similar concurrent microbatches.
dmitri: Hmm interesting. So the coordinator would dedupe overlapping hints and issue a single warmup? How heavy is the coordination?
meera: Lightweight: scheduler emits warm_candidate(tenant, model, shard, ts, score). Coordinator aggregates for short windows (~5ms), collapses overlaps, and issues a warm_request(batch_id, ranges, priority, revocable=true). Allocator receives batch requests, tries to materialize pages best-effort.
joan: Two immediate questions: (1) Who owns scoring (scheduler vs coordinator)? (2) How do we prevent the coordinator from becoming a new global bottleneck?
meera: Scoring stays local in scheduler (cheap heuristics: prefix matched, route frequency, cache misses). Coordinator only aggregates and dedupes. It should be sharded by pool/NUMA node to avoid global hotspots.
alex: From allocator side: we need clear contract for revocable memory. If warm_request is revocable, allocator should mark allocations as "soft-resident" and eligible for immediate eviction under pressure. We also need an admission token to bill tenant for warm IO.
dmitri: Agree on soft-resident. Also implement a lease: warm_request(ttl_ms) so allocator can retire entries automatically. And a cancel API for coordinator to retract if it decides to deprioritize.
meera: Good call on TTL. Example API sketch: 
```ncoordinator.emit(candidate={tenant:,model:,shard:,offsets:,score:})
allocator.warm_request(batch_id, ranges, priority, ttl_ms, revocable) -> lease_token
allocator.cancel_lease(lease_token)
```
meera: We should also define priority buckets mapped to admission tiers: realtime(high), interactive(medium), background(low). Coordinator maps scores->buckets.
sam_ops: ops note: be mindful of cross-host warmups creating network IO spikes. If coordinator dedupes across hosts, it might trigger bursty NVMe reads. Gate with pacing and per-host concurrency limits.
joan: We must avoid false-positive warming that fragments host staging. Warmed ranges should prefer contiguous ranges to reduce fragmentation. Coordinator should favor coalesced ranges.
dmitri: Telemetry we need: requests issued, dedupe rate, warmed bytes, revocations, warm hit-rate (page present on touch), extra eviction churn caused by warming. Also correlate with tail latency percentiles.
alex: Implementation plan: prototype coordinator as an opt-in subsystem behind flag that runs in the scheduler agent. Start with single-pool coordinator (canary). Add allocator hooks for soft-resident tagging + lease tokens.
meera: Rollout idea: enable for small-chat models on a couple low-traffic hosts; run A/B with trace-level telemetry. Perf target: reduce host->gpu fault p99 by 30% for 1-8 token microbatches.
joan: Edgecases: what if warm_request races with eviction compaction? Need a cheap backoff: if allocator receives warm_request for ranges currently being compacted, it should NACK with retry-after. Coordinator then reschedules.
dmitri: Also handle tenant fairness: include tenant in rate-limit key and integrate with admission quotas. High-volume tenants shouldn't drown out others.
sam_ops: Add a hard cap on warmed bytes per-host and per-tenant per-epoch. Ops will tune caps in canary.
alex: Sounds reasonable. I'll draft an RFC with diagrams: message flow (scheduler->coordinator->allocator), lease lifecycle, priority mapping, telemetry matrix, and rollout plan. @meera can you include sample scoring heuristics? @dmitri can you add allocator hook sketches?
meera: Yep, I'll assemble heuristics tomorrow.
dmitri: I'll stub allocator APIs and a small prototype.
infra-bot: perf-bot: Please attach initial microbench numbers to the RFC to baseline canary.
meera: Will do. Thanks everyone. :sparkles:
